regime_context: The detector shows a one-narrative regime in Canada/TSX, with Oil & Gas Producers (XEG.TO) as the dominant, eligible, scorable leader (score 1.91, durability 0.71, breadth 0.929, crowded). Rotation breadth is narrowing (0.38 eligible), but only the absolute-trend gate has validated edge here (gate_helps=true). I take this as a stay-with-the-leader-if-it-holds-trend regime, not a predictive one.
emerging_watch: Watching whether Gold Miners (XGD.TO, score 1.015, challenger) can convert its near-leadership into eligibility=true and a durability_bar above 0.5; the condition to retire this watch is Gold Miners reaching eligible=true with breadth above 0.4 for 10 consecutive trading days.

theses.subject: Oil & Gas Producers
theses.thesis: XEG.TO is the only theme that is simultaneously eligible, the rotation leader, highest durability (0.71), highest breadth (0.929), and one-narrative dominant. The trend-gate leg (the one validated edge on this market) is protecting it. I stay long the trend while it holds, without treating the rank as alpha.
evidence: crowded true (size-down caution only, not a fade)
theses.dissent: Crowding_z 1.19 plus one_narrative=true means the theme is consensus; attention spikes often mark tops, so any fundamental oil-price shock could produce a sharp unwind.

falsifier.text: XEG.TO closes below its 50-day average and Oil & Gas Producers drops from eligible=true to eligible=false before the check-by date

theses.subject: Big Banks
theses.thesis: Big Banks are the only other eligible theme with durability (0.63) and a 'trend' hurst tag, but non-crowded and not the leader. It is a supporting long while the trend-gate holds eligibility.
theses.dissent: Banks have weak breadth (0.429) and low score (0.635); Canada rate-cutting could compress net interest margins and stall the trend.

falsifier.text: ZEB.TO lags XEG.TO by more than 5% and Big Banks loses eligibility=true before the check-by date

theses.subject: Uranium & Nuclear
theses.thesis: Uranium & Nuclear is ineligible, score -1.913, breadth 0.0, and durability 0.18. It is the weakest theme in the set and shows no trend-gate protection, so I avoid it entirely.
theses.dissent: Uranium has periodic supply-driven spikes that the detector would miss because it is a mean-reverter with no breadth; a geopolitical supply disruption could outperform.

falsifier.text: Uranium & Nuclear becomes eligible=true with breadth above 0.5 before the check-by date
